title: They’re pancakes. Just pancakes.
body:
The breakfast special does not include a prophecy. Please stop asking me to interpret your pancakes.

If the syrup happens to spell something, turn the plate around and carry on eating.

title: A note about returns
body:
Books should be returned in the condition in which they were purchased. Being haunted is not considered ordinary wear.

If a book has begun whispering, please bring it to the counter. Do not teach it your address.

title: Regarding the howling
body:
Whoever is howling after midnight: some of us have work in the morning.

This is a request for consideration, not an invitation to form a choir.
signature: A tired resident of Maple Grove

title: Community gardening morning
body:
Volunteers welcome on Saturday morning. Please bring gloves, a trowel and clearly labelled plants.

I cannot spend another morning identifying which ones bite. If yours requires a muzzle, kindly mention that before we unload it.

title: One umbrella. Very independent.
body:
Found walking down Main Street without its owner. Black handle, excellent manners, strongly opposed to being folded.

Please collect it before the weather improves and it decides to go sightseeing.
signature: Left with the town hall’s lost property

title: A mirror with opinions
body:
A lovely dressing mirror has arrived at Second Chances. Beautiful frame, a little silvering at the edges, and very generous with compliments.

Please do not ask it to settle an argument. We have only just persuaded the last customers to leave.

title: The kettle is on
body:
If you find yourself passing Number 5 Maple Grove, do knock. There is usually tea, and I have made rather more biscuits than one person can reasonably eat.

Please use the front door. The garden gate and I are not currently on speaking terms.

title: A small correction
body:
The shape in your coffee is supposed to be a leaf.

It is not a warning, an omen or a portrait of your neighbour. I am practising. Please be encouraging.

title: Signatures, please
body:
Please read the whole document before signing it. This includes the small print, the footnotes and any clauses that attempt to move to the next page.

A reassuring smile is not a substitute for legal advice. Even mine.

title: Has anyone seen Agnes?
body:
Has anyone seen Agnes Hart today? I called at Number 5 and couldn’t get an answer.

If she’s stopped in with one of you, would you ask her to let us know she’s all right?

title: Agnes hasn’t been in
body:
Agnes hasn’t stopped by the diner, and I haven’t heard from her.

Has anyone spoken to her since yesterday? Please leave a message if you know where she is.

title: Still no word?
body:
I’ve checked at the shop and along Maple Grove. No sign of Agnes.

If anyone has heard from her, please let Margaret know.

title: Regarding Agnes Hart
body:
A reminder that the community board is intended for official notices.

That said, I understand everyone’s concern. We are looking into Agnes’s whereabouts. If you have seen or heard from her, please let me know directly. I will post an update as soon as there is news.

title: Sad news about Agnes Hart
body:
It is with great sadness that I must let everyone know that Agnes Hart was found in her car at the town border in the early hours of this morning. She had sadly passed away.

I know how many of you have been looking for her and hoping for good news. I am so sorry to bring you this instead. Please look after one another today.

title: Agnes Hart’s funeral
body:
Agnes’s funeral will be held the following weekend. Everyone in Cedar Hollow is welcome to attend and pay their respects.

She gave so much of herself to this community. Let us come together to remember her with the same kindness she showed us.

title: Rest in peace, Agnes
body:
I keep expecting you to come through the door.

Thank you for every kind word and every time you made an ordinary day feel a little better. You are already missed.

title: Your usual place
body:
There are people who make a place feel warmer just by being in it. Agnes was one of them.

The diner won’t feel quite the same without her. Rest peacefully, dear friend.

title: Forever missed
body:
Some people leave a space in a town that nobody else can fill.

Thank you for the kindness, the conversations and the countless small things, Agnes. You will be remembered on Maple Grove and far beyond it.

title: All the little things
body:
It is the little things I find myself remembering: a conversation that lasted longer than planned, a familiar smile, the way you always had time for someone.

I wish we had a little more time, Agnes.

title: A neighbour and a friend
body:
Agnes Hart was part of the heart of this community. Her kindness will be remembered long after the flowers have faded.

My thoughts are with everyone who loved her.

title: Maple Grove remembers
body:
A few of us have been sharing our memories of Agnes. Somehow, every story comes back to a moment when she made someone feel less alone.

What a lovely thing to leave behind.

title: Flowers for Agnes
body:
Thank you to everyone who has left flowers and kind words in Agnes’s memory.

Please make room for one another when you stop to remember her. There are many people who have something to say goodbye to.

title: Thinking of you, Agnes
body:
There is never enough time with the people who make a town feel like home.

You will be missed, Agnes. More than these few words can say.

title: Still thinking of you
body:
I caught myself thinking, “I must tell Agnes.”

It will take a while to stop doing that. Perhaps I never quite will.

title: A cup for an old friend
body:
Today I’m remembering the conversations that began with “just a quick cup” and lasted far longer.

I would happily let the coffee go cold for one more of those.

title: Kindness stays
body:
A town is made of its people and all the small kindnesses they leave behind.

Agnes left us plenty to carry on. Let’s remember to do that.

title: Not forgotten
body:
The board will fill with other notices in time. That doesn’t mean we have stopped remembering.

Rest in peace, Agnes. You are part of this place.

title: Thank you, Cedar Hollow
body:
Thank you for the care you have shown one another, and for every memory of Agnes you have shared.

Let us keep looking after our neighbours. I can think of no better way to honour her.

title: A welcome for our newest resident
body:
Please join me in welcoming Oliver Hart, Agnes’s great-nephew, to Number 5 Maple Grove.

I hope everyone will offer him a warm welcome and treat him with the kindness and generosity Agnes showed us over the years. Let us help him feel at home.

title: Back to the usual questions
body:
Yes, we still have pancakes. No, I still cannot tell your future from them.

Come in, have something warm and be kind to whoever ends up in the next booth.

category: A note from your new neighbour
title: Hello, Maple Grove
body:
Hello, everyone. I’m Oliver, the new face at Number 5.

Thank you for making me feel welcome. If you see me standing outside looking as though I’ve forgotten why I came out, I’m probably still trying to remember where I packed something.

title: A bookshop reminder
body:
A reminder that a bookmark is the preferred way to keep your place.

If you have left something less ordinary between the pages, please collect it. We are running out of suitable drawers.

title: One last box. Possibly.
body:
Does anyone have a reliable method for finding the one thing you need in a house full of boxes?

Please note that “remember where you put it” has already been suggested.

title: Has my cake tin followed you home?
body:
If you borrowed my round cake tin, could you please bring it back?

If you did not borrow it, but have found it waiting hopefully on your doorstep, please bring it back anyway. It has become rather used to being returned with something inside.

An empty tin and a thank-you will do perfectly well. Do not let it negotiate.

title: The teaspoons are not souvenirs
body:
A small request: please stop taking the café teaspoons home.

If they are getting into your pockets by themselves, please check before you leave. I cannot keep explaining to customers why we are stirring coffee with a soup spoon.

Also, the latte art is still a leaf. Thank you.

title: One teapot. A considerable repertoire.
body:
A charming little teapot is looking for a new home. Floral pattern, excellent spout, whistles beautifully.

Unfortunately, it does not wait for the water to boil. Requests are welcome, though it has very firm opinions about the chorus.

Please collect before it teaches the other crockery to harmonise.

title: You do not have to bring anything
body:
If someone invites you in for a cup of tea, you are allowed to arrive without a cake, a gift or an apology for being a bother.

Your company is quite enough. Though if you happen to leave with a slice of pie, I would appreciate the plate back eventually.

title: A word about the pumpkins
body:
A reminder that choosing a pumpkin does not require an expert panel, three competing opinions and a second visit to inspect the other side.

Having said that, this year’s are particularly good. Possibly my best yet.

Anyone heard saying that I said that last year is welcome to admire how consistent I am.

title: A very happy Halloween, Cedar Hollow
body:
Wishing all our residents a very happy Halloween. Enjoy the costumes, admire the pumpkins and look after one another while you celebrate.

And please do not fill up on too much candy. Yes, that reminder is for the grown-ups as well.

A little moderation now will leave you far more comfortable tomorrow. Have a lovely evening, everyone.

title: One scarf, not a trail marker
body:
I have found a knitted scarf with a very determined collection of leaves attached.

If it is yours, please describe the colour when you ask me for it. The leaves will not be a reliable means of identification by then.

Thank you to everyone taking their litter home. The woods do not need souvenirs of your lunch.

title: A small correction to this morning’s broadcast
body:
Good morning, Cedar Hollow. For the benefit of Arthur Bell, who has already made his feelings admirably clear: it was not, in fact, twenty past whenever-you-like.

The clocks are blameless. The presenter is considering his position.

Elias, if this becomes tomorrow’s headline, I expect to be credited as your source.

title: It is not a box of rubbish
body:
The box of small parts beside my workbench is a box of small parts.

It is not rubbish. It is not a collection for the thrift shop. And it is certainly not improved by somebody tidying it into a different box without telling me.

I knew exactly where everything was. Approximately.

title: A small matter of glitter
body:
If you are returning borrowed craft supplies, please put the lids on before putting them in the bag.

The intention was for the decorations to sparkle. The inside of my coat was not part of the project.

Thank you to everyone who remembered. I know precisely who you are.

title: An entirely respectable bookmark
body:
A bookmark does not have to be beautiful, expensive or even intended as a bookmark.

It should, however, preferably not be a slice of toast.

Whoever left the evidence between chapters six and seven may collect their crumbs. I shall be keeping my opinion of the practice.

title: The calendar is not a guest complaint
body:
I have been asked whether Friday the thirteenth affects the quality of the beds.

It does not.

Drowse has tested his usual chair at considerable length and reports no difficulties, though I cannot claim to have received his findings in writing.

The coffee remains excellent. Please try not to spill it while blaming the date.

title: The list would help
body:
I am always happy to help you find the thing you came in for.

If your description is “the usual thing, in the packet, somewhere near the other thing”, we may need to make an afternoon of it.

Do bring your shopping list. Remembering to write one and remembering to take it with you are separate achievements.

title: A very brief reminder
body:
This notice is not an accusation.

It is simply a cheerful opportunity to remember where you put the dental floss.

If you have just looked away from the board rather quickly, I shall choose to believe you have gone to find it.

title: A compliment is not a collection order
body:
To the lovely person who said the cake in the window was too pretty to eat: thank you.

To everyone who has repeated this and then asked for a slice: I understand completely.

Please do not feel obliged to preserve the decoration for posterity. I promise I would rather it made somebody happy than spent the week being admired from a distance.

title: A convenient explanation
body:
If you arrive late and explain that Felix gave you the time, I shall sympathise.

If you use this explanation twice, I shall recommend a clock.

If you use it a third time, I shall begin to suspect that the radio is not the difficulty.
signature: Arthur Bell · The Ticking Time Peace
